To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pigeons' responding maintained the postponement of time-outs from a schedule of reinforcement when such responding did not decrease timeout frequency or increase the frequency of food reinforcement.
pigeons' responding postponed timeouts from a food reinforcement schedule, even though responding neither decreased the frequency of the timeouts nor increased the frequency of food reinforcement.

pigeons can maintain responding that postpones timeouts from a schedule of reinforcement when such responding (a) neither decreases overall timeout frequency nor (b) increases overall frequency of food delivery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of reinforcement in the control of behavior that postpones the occurrence of timeout periods.
the effects of postponement of a timeout period on the maintenance of a response that postpones it.
a form of behavior that is not readily accommodated by traditional reinforcement accounts of the control of operant behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pigeons will maintain responding to postpone timeouts, even if such responding decreases overall timeout frequency and increases overall reinforcement rate.

the results of the present experiments do not support the hypothesis that the effects of timeout postponement are mediated by an increase in the overall frequency with which food reinforcement is available.

the results of these experiments indicate that pigeons will maintain behavior that postpones a timeout from a schedule of reinforcement when that behavior neither decreases overall timeout frequency nor increases overall food reinforcement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

postponement of extinction periods is a robust form of behavioral control that can be maintained in the absence of increases in overall food-reinforcement frequency or increases in the frequency of food-correlated stimuli.
postponing timeout from a schedule of positive reinforcement is maintained by a reduction of the negative effects of timeout, not by the positive effects of food.
postponing a timeout is a form of behavior that can be negatively reinforced in its own right.
The main takeaway from our work is that
timeout postponement is a robust effect that is not dependent on either an increase in food reinforcement or an increase in the frequency of food-correlated stimuli.
the contingencies that maintain responding during extinction can be complex and that extinction procedures should be carefully designed to avoid the unintended reinforcement of extinction responding.
